memoryReview.evidence: apps/emergent-kingdoms/visual-direction.json; architecture and composition reviewed; screenshots not available for comparison
memoryReview.lesson: Avoid copying the geographic simulation station with a permanent measurement journal; tactical orders need a collapsible inset command sheet and direct route gestures.

memoryReview.evidence: apps/palimpsest-atlas/visual-direction.json; architecture and composition reviewed; screenshots not available for comparison
memoryReview.lesson: A permanent timeline beneath an inset map serves documented history but duplicates the earlier Banners layout; keep the world continuous beneath contextual controls.
Maintain a single dominant physical scene, but distinguish temporary tactical drafts from committed physical changes; do not transplant the sculpture's discrete placement interaction.

references.observation: Formation silhouettes and movement frontage provide an immediate spatial representation of military posture.
references.principle: Represent the geometry of the actual command instead of hiding all information behind troop statistics.
references.application: Show the intended footprint at each planned endpoint and preserve the echelon of each regiment during a group turn.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce the Napoleonic formation modifiers or copy another game's sprites or graphical style.

references.observation: Planned orders are drawn over the map and both sides act during the same resolved time interval.
references.principle: The planned route and the executed movement must be visually distinct while remaining spatially connected.
references.application: Use dashed numbered paths, projected footprints, and deterministic playback for individual and grouped orders.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce the exact arrow art or assume the reference rules fit a medieval battlefield.

references.observation: The map guide treats contours, water courses and woodland tint as different geographic layers.
references.principle: Terrain marks should convey the physical cause of movement constraints and remain subordinate to unit marks.
references.application: Render procedural contours and wooded clusters below high-contrast heraldic pennants and command strokes.
references.avoid: Do not reproduce USGS source map imagery, real topography or modern official surveying symbol sets verbatim.

concepts.medium: Procedural Canvas ink atlas with small geometric rank marks and authored vector pennants.
concepts.composition: Continuous battlefield under inset status and collapsible command sheet; portrait rotates the map by ninety degrees.
concepts.interaction: Tap a regiment and draw its route directly in the landscape; reveal or fold the command sheet when needed.
concepts.motion: A dashed route appears immediately, followed by measured acceleration and physical contact during replay.
concepts.rationale: The map communicates geometry, terrain and timing without covering most of the phone with a permanent dossier.

concepts.medium: Low polygon 3D soldiers and terrain with physically lit materials and authored skeletal movement.
concepts.composition: Perspective view of the front line with a camera orbit and a row of selected regiment portraits.
concepts.interaction: Select a miniature regiment in perspective and place a destination marker using camera-relative ray casting.
concepts.motion: Continuous walk and weapon animation with camera-driven changes in silhouette and depth perception.
concepts.rationale: More expressive combat depiction but costly and visually ambiguous when drawing exact paths on a small display.

concepts.medium: Crisp SVG military diagram using block symbols and explicit annotated contact and morale tracks.
concepts.composition: Two-column staff document with an order-of-battle ledger beside a schematic network of tactical lanes.
concepts.interaction: Edit a table of chained commands and reorder stages rather than draw gestures over terrain.
concepts.motion: Discrete state transitions, animated order lines and static small multiples of the tactical front.
concepts.rationale: Excellent for formal order programming but weak for direct movement through continuous terrain and frontage.

selection.reason: Direct map drawing and readable planned footprints are the central interaction; continuous battlefield and collapsible controls preserve that precision on a phone.

rejected.reason: Perspective foreshortening complicates exact frontage and group route drawing and substantially increases the asset and device performance burden.
A document-first workflow hides the spatial relationships needed for encirclement, flank exposure and independent regiment movement.

tools.reason: The implemented browser Canvas renderer supports procedural contours, soldier ranks, future route overlays and deterministic map playback.
Existing product-specific vector icon can be rendered directly by browsers without downloading font or raster art assets.
Universal QA captured actual Chromium and WebKit mobile and desktop frames in run 45300337365; final build still requires separate sign-off.
No Blender workflow was exercised because this release changes top-down map interaction rather than authored 3D subjects.
tools.fallback: Keep the lightweight Canvas rank representation, which is adequate for the explicitly selected diagrammatic map medium.

assets.role: Procedural terrain geometry is consumed by the runtime Canvas atlas renderer, with hill contours, rivers, woodland and ford.
assets.acceptance: The battlefield is readable without overlays and planned paths are distinguishable from terrain marks at phone and desktop scale.
assets.integration: Terrain geometry is defined in the engine; the app draws and caches the raster field in memory. No external file request is required.
assets.provenance: Original procedural implementation in this repository, inspired by cartographic principles rather than imported visual assets.

assets.role: Forked banner silhouettes identify regiment and app identity at small dimensions; the install icon is an authored vector.
assets.acceptance: Two crossing standards in the install icon and high-contrast unit pennants remain recognizable at launcher and map sizes.
assets.integration: Canvas draws individual rank marks and flags; the existing SVG is declared in the manifest and cached by the service worker.
assets.provenance: Original app-owned SVG icon and procedural Canvas flags; no external graphic or type asset copied.

assets.role: Connected heightfield terrain, directional shaded relief, roads, forest canopy and sector-based miniature armies.
assets.acceptance: Four terrain archetypes, same deterministic geometry at all three camera scales, actual physical strips represented in rank positions.
assets.integration: Runtime terrain generator and cached Canvas rendering, with an app-local module worker for the physics.
assets.provenance: Original procedural assets and code; no third-party artwork.

risks: Command sheet can cover the enemy front on small screens; verify fitted battlefield bounds after opening and closing.
Dense ranks and labels may overlap; check path planning and replay at both browser engines.
Layout readbacks during render may harm frame time; cache geometry and inspect measured performance.
Detailed focus exposes raster sampling and troop readability; inspect close warrior screenshot after increasing zoom.
Offline WebKit navigation requires a complete activated versioned cache including the module worker.
comparisons: Compare mobile before/after frame for map coverage and control legibility.
Compare desktop after selecting a regiment and after executing the same order chain.
